source: AI Video Bootcamp - two real, distinct lessons, applied together: 'Image Editing With Nanobanana' (Phase 3, transcript31.pdf) - 'you can take an existing photo, type in a plain English prompt and watch the image transform... turn the lighting dramatic and the red tone', and 'you can change the perspective of any image perfectly with a prompt like this' - the relighting/re-angling-an-existing-photo half; and 'Creating AI Avatars' (Phase 3, transcript.pdf + Creating AI Avatars.txt) - its character turnaround-sheet technique ('FRONT VIEW, 0 degree rotation... 45 DEGREE LEFT TURN... 90 DEGREE LEFT PROFILE... 90 DEGREE RIGHT PROFILE... 45 DEGREE RIGHT TURN... BACK VIEW, 180 degree rotation', all from one reference image) - the multi-angle-from-one-reference half. Neither lesson names a single 'relight-and-angles' technique; this bank is an honest synthesis of the two, not a transcription of one unified lesson.
note: No new vocabulary lives here - every lighting/angle phrase is resolved through the EXISTING tools/lighting_bank.json (build_lighting.compose_lighting) and tools/camera_angle_bank.json (build_camera_angle.compose_camera_angle) at build time, so this bank can never drift out of sync with those two gates. `sets` are named shot lists for tools/build_relight.py. The turnaround-sheet lesson used literal degree rotations (0/45/90/180); the closest match in this app's own camera-angle vocabulary is the `sides` axis (frontal/three-quarter/profile/back-shot), so `avatar-turnaround` maps onto that rather than inventing a separate degree-based axis the rest of the app does not share. `relight-pass` and `full-set` are this bank's own combinations built from the two lessons' vocabulary, not lesson content themselves.

avatar-turnaround.label: Avatar turnaround (angle only, 4 shots)
avatar-turnaround.source_note: Creating AI Avatars' turnaround-sheet technique, mapped onto the existing side axis (frontal/three-quarter/profile/back-shot) in place of literal degree rotations.

relight-pass.label: Relight pass (lighting only, 4 shots)
relight-pass.source_note: NanoBanana's existing-photo relighting demo ('turn the lighting dramatic and the red tone'), applied across four of tools/lighting_bank.json's own named setups - the camera angle is left untouched in every shot.

full-set.label: Full set (lighting and angle together, 4 shots)
full-set.source_note: Both lessons combined, one distinct (lighting, angle) pair per shot - for when a user wants full range rather than isolating one variable at a time.
